subject: Communication
title: Confirmation Bias: The Filter You Don't See
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Confirmation Bias: The Filter You Don't See.

hook.text: You Google a question and click the first result that agrees with you. The other nine? Invisible.

buildup.text: Confirmation bias is the tendency to seek, favor, and remember information that confirms your existing beliefs.

discovery.text: It's not just what you seek. It's what you notice: your brain literally filters out information that contradicts your beliefs.

twist.text: The smarter you are, the better you are at rationalizing your biases. Intelligence amplifies bias, not corrects it.

climax.text: The antidote: actively seek opposing viewpoints. Read the source you disagree with most.

punchline.text: You're not objective. Nobody is. Knowing that is the first step.

quiz.question: How does intelligence affect confirmation bias?
options: Intelligence can amplify it through better rationalization

details.summary: Confirmation bias makes you seek, interpret, and remember information that confirms your existing beliefs while ignoring contradictory evidence. It operates below conscious awareness, making your information diet systematically skewed without you realizing it.
details.whyItMatters: Confirmation bias is the most powerful obstacle to accurate understanding. It turns information consumption into belief reinforcement rather than learning.
takeaways: You naturally seek information that confirms existing beliefs
Contradictory evidence is unconsciously filtered out
It operates below awareness, making self-correction difficult

faq.question: Can intelligent people overcome confirmation bias?
faq.answer: Intelligence does not protect against confirmation bias; it can actually make it worse. Smarter people are better at rationalizing beliefs they already hold. The most effective defense is deliberate exposure to high-quality opposing viewpoints combined with intellectual humility.

faq.question: How does social media amplify confirmation bias?
faq.answer: Algorithms learn what you engage with and show you more of the same, creating a feedback loop between your bias and your feed. You see increasingly extreme versions of your existing views. The result is that social media can transform mild preferences into rigid convictions.
